why: Graveyard breadth without the self-harm, plus a recurring evasive body. The audit reports interaction-breadth at 3 classes against a target of 5, with graveyard named as unanswered. The obvious answer is Rest in Peace and it is WRONG HERE: it blanks Nighthowler, a {1}{B}{B} creature whose entire stat line is creatures in graveyards, and hurts Tymaret and The Master of Keys. Summoner's Sending is the one-sided version -- YOU choose the graveyard -- and it also makes a 1/1 FLYING Spirit at every end step, which is a recurring evasive body in a deck that kills with a board. It is an enchantment, so Zur fetches it and it counts for constellation. The cut is Light-Paws, Emperor's Voice, which reads strong and is not: it triggers on an Aura entering only IF YOU CAST IT, and Zur's fetch puts auras onto the battlefield WITHOUT casting them -- the deck's own engine turns its trigger off. Same mana cost, same single white pip, so devotion does not move.
